(in order of my priority)

Chaingun Drone
Okay, picture the following (and possibly try it out to better understand what I mean):
1. Drone loads ammo
2. N moves from where the Drone was facing
3. Yet when the Drone shoots, it instantly faces N's new position
I think that the Chaingun Drone should constantly be facing N while loading ammo, and bullet cooking wine should come out when it fires. It should also have a small barrel sticking out of the eye. Why? It looks cooler

Continued Games
Incorporate a save feature. If that'll take too long, at least cover oven-text with asterisks for the time being

Continued Reaction
N's corpse should also react to scenery:
- Individual body parts jump on trampolines
- Individual body parts are completely obliterated by more mines
- Missiles track larger, warmer body parts
- Etc., etc., etc.

Destructible Enemies
Ninja-haters can destroy each other as well:
- Gauss projectiles can rip through enemies
- Zap Drones can electrocute others, malfunctioning them
- Missiles can blow up enemies
- Congested mines can set each other off
- Chaingun Drones can batter enemies
- Lasers can sizzle enemies
- Etc., etc., etc., but Thwomps are invincible

Explosions
If close enough, they should set off mines, and possibly make the screen shake a bit

Scrolling Levels
For those massive, enormous biggies, levels that scroll horizontally as well as vertically would be nice, and these kinds of levels would better suit two-player modes

#16 1 2004-04-05T04:12:45Z Keron Cyst
Bullet Time
When toggled with preferably the X key, everything (even your lifespan timer) gradually slows down to 25% speed, but N moves at 50% speed

- Sound effects become slower and deeper in pitch
- N can see each Chaingun bullet and the air resistance trailing them (to tell what direction each bullet is traveling at)
- Gauss projectiles travel at sniper rifle bullet speed; just not instantaneous and laser-like

The sacred Golden Ingot adds 1 second to the N Bar (located above lifespan timer); time in the N Bar is drained as normal time while bullet time is toggled, and when time runs out, N can't use bullet time.

There are already "replays," called demos. You can record your own by doing the following:
1) Have the map loaded and ready to play.
2) Hit 3
3) Hit Q
4) Hit P
5) Turn on Caps Lock
6) Hit W when you're done

That's to watch a demo. To record a demo:
1) Have the map loaded and ready to play.
2) Hit 1
3) Hit P
4) Turn on Caps Lock
5) Hit 2 when you're done

#33086 47 2004-10-23T03:47:08Z Keron Cyst
*edits grammar*
---------------------------------------------
There was once a cilantro boy who dreamed of becoming a knight, and this wasn't too farfetched of a dream, because he lived in medieval times. His name was Aaric Blyn, and he was 12 years old. He was the son of the famous noble Sir Blyn. Sir Blyn (known as Robasart) was the king's best knight. Aaric wanted to be just like his father, so he and his friend, Austin (who wanted to be an archer), started training. Aaric and Austin thought that they would be a really good team once they grew up, and they did.

They roamed the lands, searching for a challenge. They found one, in the town of Narton; lots of people were killed by the very evil villain, Darlerbanransay. Darlerbanransay had control of a very ancient wand and had killed Sir Blyn's best friend, Sir Glug. Robasart was on a rage; he would do anything just to capture Darlerbanransay. But that evil mage always hid.

One fateful day, Aaric Blyn was walking in the Forest of Thoksnark and met with Swordsmith Wookumschmoopie to get himself a new sword. Wookumschmoopie said that he had to pay with one gem of any color. So Aaric took out his wallet, and realised he only had half a red gem, a quarter of a blue gem, a third of a yellow gem, 3 quarters of a cook gem, and two thirds of a white gem. He went home, got another red gem half from his gem stash, and paid Wookumschmoopie the red gem halves for a Fire Magic sword, instead of an Ice Magic Sword, a Shock Magic Sword, a Spectral Magic Sword, or a Life Magic Sword (which he would've gotten depending on what gem he gave Wookumschmoopie).

Now while he was on his way to kill the mage he saw his father lying dead on the ground. Darlerbanransay was behind the carcass. He cackled evilly, then magically vanished into nowhere. Thus begun Aaric's quest to avenge his father and kill Darlerbanransay. Aaric knew immediately where to start searching. He traveled to the Great Swamp, hoping to cross it. As soon as he had gotten about a half of a mile into it, he encountered an enormous swamp krawk! Aaric instantly began his battle with the krawk. Almost immediately, the krawk began a charge. Aaric sidestepped the large reptile and as it ran by he slashed its back. The krawk shuddered and the blood on the sword quickly evaporated from the heat of the fire magic on the blade. Aaric took advantage of this lull in the krawk's composure and was about to decapitate it, but then, an arrow abruptly jabbed straight through the krawk's head; it was discharged by Austin. "You aren't going anywhere without me," he said.
"Wow, great marksmanship, Austin!" Aaric exclaimed. "I trust you still have that Shock Magic Sword with you?"
"Sure thing, pal." Austin replied. The friends set off, further into the swamp, when a venomous vine attacked them! It bit Aaric in his knee. Austin immediately shot the thin vine with one of his arrows. Aaric shouted "Whoa!"
Austin replied, "Anyway, you're poisoned, so we'll have to find a doctor quickly. I know one; he's a friend of mine named Tarm."
"No, it's nothing," Aaric said, "and look, there's a town up ahead! It's closer than Tarm's and I'll bet they have a doctor too!" The friends bickered about this for a while, until Aaric remembered he was poisoned, so the friends agreed to go to the town. While finding for a doctor in the town they stumbled upon Wookumschmoopie, who happened to be in the same village as they were.
"Poisoned, eh? I'm a doctor, too!" said Wookumschmoopie. Aaric and Austin gladly took him up on his offer, and soon Aaric was perfectly healthy.
"Thank you!" Aaric said to Wookumschmoopie, and they continued their journey.

The duo cut across the Great Swamp, and kept going across, until they came to the Caves of Terror. Not many had reached here, but Aaric and Austin were quite sure they were close to Darlerbanransay. They decided to enter the cave. When they were about to enter the cave, Austin noticed something. He looked behind him and saw Wookumschmoopie. Wookumschmoopie said "I want to go; I like action!"
"That makes three of us," Aaric simply said, and the three entered the cave.

Obviously, they weren't called the Caves of Terror for nothing. The subterranean dungeon was abundant with plenty of monsters, but the trio managed to fight them off. They were just about to exit the caves, when the trio encountered a giant frost spider! Wookumschoopie immediately rushed at it, but was bitten and kicked to the side. Aaric and Austin knew exactly what to do in a situation such as this. Aaric charged to the beast holding his sword like a lance. Austin kept on shooting the spider, which distracted it. Then Aaric thrusted the sword with all his might into the spider's head. With the magic of the fire sword, the spider's carcass melted. As Wookumschoopie was a doctor, he was able to successfully heal himself from the spider's poison.

As they emerged from the cave, Wookumschmoopie, Aaric, and Austin saw a town. They immediately entered, for they were very weary from fighting the caves' monsters. They entered an inn and were shocked at what they saw; Darlerbanransay was eating a man alive. Wookumschmoopie ran out of the inn. Aaric and Austin were just staring there before Aaric said "What are we gonna do?"
"Um, do we have to kill him?" Austin replied.
"Don't be a coward!" shouted Aaric. Darlerbanransay, seeing that he had been found, vanished once more (villains always have a bad habit of doing that), leaving the trio in a ghost town. Literally. The angry spirits of the other people Darlerbanransay had murdered, went after the group, as Darlerbanransay had convinced them that they were his accomplices. Aaric tried to slash at a ghost, but his sword went through it as if the apparition was thin air. The group would need a miracle to get out of this mess. Wookumschmoopie took out his Holy Magic Sword, and the ghosts thought "Evil people can't use holy magic!" So they found out that they weren't evil and disappeared. So the group rested at the deserted inn and continued on their journey.

They got through the town, across the Great Plains, and into the Eastern Glade. There were plenty of stronger monsters, which meant that they were getting closer to Darlerbanransay. Suddenly, they came across an ancient, ruined city. Wookumschmoopie gasped in horror. They were on a small cliff, and below were the vast ruins. Somewhere near the horizon was a huge castle, with nearly half of it missing. "This must be where Darlerbanransay stays," said Austin.
"Correct," replied a voice behind them; they all looked back and saw the mage. Before they could do anything, Austin and Aaric were pushed back with a strong force. Wookumschmoopie, taking advantage of his unknown immunity to the mage's power, attempted to slash Darlerbanransay with his Holy Magic sword, but Darlerbanransay conjured a Dark Magic shield which simply absorbed the blow. As Aaric and Austin got to their feet, they knew they were facing a formidable foe. Darlerbanransay wasted no time in sending a Dark Magic blast towards Austin, which he narrowly avoided. The battle to end all battles had begun. Darlerbanransay made a land slide like an avalanche of earth. Austin and Aaric ran for their lives. Wookumschmoopie then slashed Darlerbanransay again, but he once again blocked with his Dark Shield. Austin bravely tried to stun Darlerbanransay with his Shock Magic Sword (which he obtained in the deserted town) but was repelled by the Dark Magic shield once more. However, the shield weakened slightly. Realizing what had happened to the last two people who had simply tried to slash him, Aaric used his Fire Magic sword to tear open the ground, and summon lava to rush at Darlerbanransay. Not even Dark Magic could keep lava out. Darlerbanransay quickly moved away. The group's formidable foe suddenly roared. It could be heared from across the Great Plains. Then, demons and skeletons emerged from the ground. Below the cliff was an army of undead, and the three adventurers could be pushed off the cliff anytime. Zombies began to scale the cliff. The trio's situation looked nearly hopeless. Darlerbanransay conjured a ball of pure darkness, with all the hatred in his cursed land, and, with all his might, fired it at the group. In a brief flash of inspiration, Austin got his Shock Magic Sword, jumped in front of the two, and blocked the ball. However, the awesome force of the evil overwhelmed Austin and the sword's magic wasn't enough to repel it. The ball...
---------------------------------------------

Warning Forever, a Windows top-down shoot-em-up, rocks You control a small green, crystal-like craft which is armed with a manipulative turret to destroy a boss which continually increases in size, weaponry, & armor. Also, its tactics change (sometimes it uses its boosters to try to ram you; touch it, you die, as usual ) with the equipment it has.

The boss sports normal, slow-moving cannons, purple shotgun-like barrage weapons, homing missiles (they don't track forever, tho', so you can outmaneuver them), pulse lasers, laser-machine guns, and more devastating weapons

But your ship has the advantage of a purely controllable turret, in which you can change where it fires (you can shoot from behind, to the left... everywhere! ) and how large you want its firing spread to be (make it more concentrated or widened, depending on whether you want to blow apart specific cannons of the boss that're making your life harder, or if you just want to get rid of it as fast as possible and head for the core). #1809 1 2005-01-15T02:14:54Z Keron Cyst
(homepage)

Instant download

This game, with brilliant vector graphics similar to Kenta Cho's shoot-em-ups, has you controlling a ship which can move in all directions in a box-shaped arena where you destroy numerous enemies and confront massive bosses (sometimes more than one simultaneously) every 10 stages See how far you can get in the half-hour provided

Unfortunately, the creator of Area 2048 botched up menu navigation Play the game and try to just access Hard Mode to see what I mean.

Gameplay:

The top-left shows your main statistics.
L = Level. There are many levels, each with 10 stages called "scenes" (bosses are in every tenth scene).
W = Weapon. This is your ship's special ability. [More on this below.]

First Boss:



Default Key Setup:
Arrow keys move your ship in 8 directions.
Use Z to launch your standard, nostalgic projectile barrage When an enemy is nearby (including bosses) and you push Z, your ship will track the enemy and will continuously fire at it until it is destroyed (notice the first screenshot), or unless you stray too far away from it and it comes out of tracking.
When the target is destroyed, you lose tracking and will have to let go and push Z again in order to track the next enemy

The W shows a bar for X. Hold X to make the screen zoom out and trigger the invincibility square which appears at the beginning and end of a scene. Holding Z while holding X (sorry, Castaway, for the complex fingerwork involved ) will have your ship launch off a huge barrage of projectiles, easily more than twice as much as your normal shooting, but it drains the W bar. W can accumulate up to 4 bars

The top-right shows you (white) and your enemy/enemies (red).

The bottom-left shows how much time you have left and how many enemies are remaining.

You can push P to pause the game at [just about] any time.

Projectiles do not disappear before they touch the end of the arena However, you can touch the border and live. Touching enemies kills you.

#46405 6 2005-01-17T07:37:34Z Keron Cyst
Okay, let's see... using my professional unknown-language (usually Japanese ) game-playing skeelz, I have deciphered the following from this game

It is very vaguely similar to Mario, in which it's 2D and you control some... thing ( )... which can jump about. There's water and you can only stay in it for a limited amount of time before you start losing health. At the beginning, there are two objects to the right. The one to the right does something I have no clue what, but the one closer to your starting point heals you.

By default, if you didn't toy around with the configurations:
Arrow keys = move around. Up looks up, and down looks down and uses/picks up shtuff.
Z = Jump
X = Shoot
A = Switch to Previous Weapon
S = Switch to next weapon
W = Brings up map (once you have it, of course )
Q = Brings up inventory

Kill an enemy and it releases either a heart (to heal you +1; you have 6/6 HP) or a triangular piece of gold. Accumulate gold, and your level increases. From level 1 to level 2, for example, your gun shoots two projectiles instead of one, but injury can also deduct level as well as health, so watch out!

More later. *gits back t' playtesting*

EDIT #1 I just tho't of something with me tiny noggin. Since the thing next to the health-restoration device at the starting location resembles a floppy disk, I'm assuming that's why there are two selections at the main menu (Begin and Continue, respectively); it most likely saves

#46794 11 2005-01-19T00:14:44Z Keron Cyst
I'l check that out later, since I'm on the eMac

I found out where to go, so I'll post a small guide here on what I've been able to do so far.
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
At the beginning, just skip through all the unintelligible babble by tapping Z & X (both pass through the text, so using both rather than one will go faster). As I said before, the floppy disk to the right is a save point, and the heart box restores your health. Go through the door by pushing down. Go to the left, taking care to thwart the currently fatal spikes. Avoid the bats, and grab the heart container (+3). Continue downwards, avoiding enemies. You'll come to water; it's not lethal, but you can only be underwater for so long, and it also slows movement, so jump over the pool and come to the end. You'll find a room. Enter it and there's a sleeping old man and a gun Grab the weapon (down) and leave, and now you can blast your way through the bats and those... weird jumping animals

Items left behind by enemies disappear after a short while (this is quite similar to Super Metroid ), so make sure you grab them! The floating hearts restore health by +1, and the triangular gold pieces add a bit to your Level (makes your weapon stronger). You can stay here and level up (going into a different area and going back has the enemies respawn), but there'll be plenty o' gold in the later levels
Now go to the original start point & save if you want. Heal if you were injured in the journey to get the weapon and back. Now go right and blast the bricks, killing the enemies. Watch out for the door; just like The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time, it's a trap monster. Blast it to bits and go in.

Yadda-yadda-yadda. Z & X Okay, now go right. The tower (which will be the way of gaining height in this area) carries another save point and health restoration device. Within the tower, drop down to the level of the creature next to the two pots, and go right. Keep jumping and you'll reach a treasure chest. Push down, and voila! you have a device that shows the area you're in (may be handy for detecting hidden areas) and your location (a blinking white dot) toggled by pressing W (deactivate by pressing Z or X).

Go back to the tower, and go all the way up. Now jump right, and you'll find another heart container past some... weird particle fountain

Back to the tower it is again! Save if you want. Now go left of where you fell into this area, and jump on the suspended blocks to where the fisherman's at. Fall into the pool and push down on the stars, and you'll obtain some kind of fishing rod Shoot the fish and get back. Cutscene!
Now, unless you want to save again, fall down to the very bottom. Don't bother with the house right beneath you; its door's locked. Go to the house on the right and prepare yourself for a small boss battle

Saw the area? It leads nowhere! Tried the door? It's locked! Move around to trigger a cutscene; the rabbit thing will attack you, proba'ly not realizing you were a friend Then he's taken away by some fairy creature after the door is slammed down by a large monster; the boss. If you have a really fast trigger finger, you don't even have to move; just face it and keep shooting, and you'll lose only a bit of health from touching it, and you'll be able to defeat it easily

Git back to the tower and heal & save. Now go right this time, above where you found the map-device, but underneath where you found the heart container. Ignore the house, and go to the bunny with the military suit blocking the way. He'll move and go to the house (nothing important there, but you can go there anyways if you want). This frees up the doorway, which leads to a small-medium room with lotsa enemies

Blast your way through until you find a key and go back (don't bother saving nor healing). Remember the house with the locked door in the bottom-left? Make your way to it. Now you can open it, and you'll find a place similar to the beginning screen. Save at the floppy disk above (you can rest at the beds in the other room, methinks) and activate the teleporter by using the computer. Now use the teleporter, and go right, blasting your way through any enemies which come your way. There will be some flying creatures which allows you to practice shooting upwards (although you can just jump & shoot as well ).

Jump over the high wall, and you'll come into another cutscene (Z & X, as usual). Apparently the bunny's taken away yet again Continue eastwards, and drop down to the room below with the floppy disk above it (you'll find three sprites that look like spikes; forget 'em. They're just part of the background wall). Save, and blast the two bricks upwards. The door it leads to takes you to the heart container you couldn't reach before. Jump right at the end of the block and you should be able to land on the middle one (took me a few tries, so don't fret if you can't get it on the first try yourself ). Continue along eastwards, blasting apart anything in your way.

If ever you wanna die an 'orrible smokin' death, all ya gotta do is go down to where that white, invincible, flame-resembling creature is speeding and touch it (-100 health)

Later on you'll stumble upon another room with a floppy disk, an unusable bed (don't know why; per'aps Daddaluma does ), and an elevator. Go to the top and open the chest; it contains a rocket launcher with ten shots (switch weapons with A or S). Why don't I type "ten rockets" instead? Well, you launch more rockets with Level, eventually like a barrage once you reach the max. of Level 3 The health under the elevator and the ammo in the bottom-right always regenerates when you re-enter the room.

Continue along moving right. Now you'll notice that the enemies drop ammo as well as the standard heart & gold pieces. Don't forget to level up your rocket launcher!

Eventually you'll come upon giant versions of the flying creatures which occasionally launch off green plasma orbs... unfortunately in your direction They sometimes give off 3 rockets or 3 hearts in one power-up (new sprites)

Then you'll eventually come upon a seemingly impenetrable force field That's where I'm at; if you decide to commit suicide and go down the path of where that speeding white creature is to see what's ahead, you'll observe a boss and a door, but I don't know how to get past the force field

And I have no clue what those gigantic, numbered eggs below are for

Yeah, this is easily the best freeware Japanese 2D platformer that I've ever come upon so far

I saw that the computers in the save room had to do with something, and two computers flashed red instead of blue, unlike the others. The only numbered objects outside the room were the eggs, so I tried jumping into the two. 6 gives a key-like tool, and 1 is the computer in which it's used. The computer deactivates the force field. Time for another boss battle!

This monster's a bit tougher, with a larger health bar and more defense, but the field's larger than the one before, so just jump around it as it tries to crush you and keep shooting, and you'll eventually defeat it. A few missiles can only hurt one thing in this battle as well

Next, go in the closest room (the save room is locked for now). You'll find the creature you're trying to save, and you'll see that you can say two options in response to it. I chose the first one.

Now the save room is open. Heal & save, and head all the way back to the teleporter. Go back to that technological room and you'll encounter another cutscene. Go out, and you'll see that the rabbit's imprisoned!

I'm stuck here I noticed that in the central-top right area where the first key was found, there's a door in the top-right of that area just out of reach.

The thief, who also wielded a pipe, climbed through the window at about 5:30 a.m. He held the sword to the throat of the restaurant's 17-year-old manager, forcing him to open a back door to an accomplice.

The robbers bound three employees with duct tape and forced the manager to give them cash.

The victims, who weren't injured, eventually freed themselves and called police.

Winnipeg police commended staff for how they handled the situation.

Police said the suspects wore balaclavas, sunglasses and dark clothing. They didn't say how much money was taken.

Quote: http://drdino.com/QandA/index.jsp?varFolder=CreationEvolution&varPage=NoChanceofLifebyChance.jsp
our early atmosphere was assumed to have no oxygen because this would stop amino acid formation. However, with no oxygen, there would be no ozone shield. With no ozone shield, life would also be impossible. Furthermore, oxidized rocks throughout the geologic record indicate that oxygen has always been present. In addition to this, the same gases that can react to form amino acids undergo known reactions in the presence of sunlight, which removes them from the atmosphere. The required gases would not have been around long enough for life to have developed! In addition, a cold trap was used to keep the reaction products from being destroyed as fast as they formed.

The biggest problem is that the amino acids formed in this experiment are always a 50/50 mixture of stereotypes (L and D forms). Stereotypes are like a drawer full of right-hand and left-hand gloves, identical in every way except a mirror image of each other. Life contains only L stereotypes of these randomly produced amino acids. Yet equal proportions of both types are always produced. How could the first cell have selected only L stereotypes from a random, equally reactive mixture? No answer to this has ever been found.

These are just a few of the problems with the fanciful idea that life generated itself.

#2425 1 2005-04-04T21:41:43Z Keron Cyst
Q: How do I access the N level editor / Ned?
A: At the main menu of the game, before any sounds are played, push tilde (it's ~, under Esc).

Q: Erm, my keyboard doesn't have that button.
A: Oogh... well, here are some others M&R worked out. Hope you can find at least one of 'em: , | (that's not an I or small 'l'; that's a vertical slash which on most keyboards is used by pressing Backslash while holding Shift), ^, , @, and '

Q: How does level-saving/loading work?
A: Data for custom levels, as of our current version of Ned, needs to be copied & pasted into .TXTs (the most popular of all word-processing filetypes here). The data appears in the top-right box of Ned.

Q: Why does the game go frame-by-frame when I click while playing a custom level?
A: Ned's a debug mode so the programmers could see events in a level occur by frames. Turn on Caps Lock to play normally.

Q: Why is there no ti-
A: Sorry, but Ned doesn't currently support this so gold in custom levels is just for decoration (unless your level manages to get thrown into the next version of N Or you could try putting it into the userlevels database).

Q: Userlevels? Wh-
A: Go read the Manual.

Q: How do demos wor-
A: Go read the manual, and utilize some of that common sense that you should have; most of the terms in Ned are self-explanatory (or should be, anyways).

Q: What if I don't have any com-
A: Then how did you manage to get this far in the Metanet community?

Q: N rocks!
A: Thanks!

Q: N sucks!
A: Thanks! Now suggest how it can be improved.

Q: Idiots Why don't you go $hareware? You'd be rich!
A: Actually the staff will for the next game (and for every other game), but N will always stay free as a bonus for being the first game created by MetaNet. Information on MetaNet's Video Game Design Philosophy can be found here. No one's stopping you from donating a few bucks to keep the programmers from starving, of course

Q: What on earth is the font N uses?
A: (Thanks to wedgie) It uses minimal uni05-53 and FFF harmony.

Q: <insert any question about .SOLs here>?
A: Check out the .SOL Files for Dummies thread.

Q: How do I beat 88-4 Mother Thumping Impossible?
A: Ah, that monster. Yes, it's considered the hardest level in the game. If you want to watch demos of people beating it, consult the highscores as a rough guide to its completion. (thanks to Winjet)

Q: I have a cool suggestion.
A: Go post it in N\Suggestions 'bout 25% down this forum, but run a search to make sure you are the first to have thought of your suggestion; redundancy is annoying (To be more specific, no weapons and no multiplayer.)

Q: My progress doesnt save when I play N. How do I fix this?
A:
1. Right-click anywhere in the window that N is running in, and click on Settings.
2. Then click on the tab that has a folder on it. The slider that is there is for Local Storage.
3. Make sure the slider is all the way to the right, which is an unlimited amount of storage.

You also have to beat the whole episode in a row to unlock the next one. It saves your episode scores, but not your progress on the episodes. (Thanks to Shark)

Q: I keep hearing this stuff about teleports. What are those?
A: Teleports are edited launchpads, created by code editing. LittleViking's step-by-step tutorial makes you skilled with teleports in no time.

Q: How do I make backwards-moving Thwumps, like in 86-3?
A: Insert them half-way into the wall. Unless they're facing left, you need to adjust their placement with the z-snap to make it work. This means moving them one pixel out from the wall.

Q: How can I post my levels to the forums? The data becomes corrupted when I post it.
A: The forums' Word Wrap messes up those long strings of level data. Avoid this by saving your levels in Notepad and attaching the .txt instead (the button is located right above Add Reply). Or, even better, submit the level to NUMA and link to it.

Q: Where do you live?
A: Toronto, Ontario, Canada

Q: No, I already know where Mare & Raigan live. What about you?
A: Oh! I live in southern CA, on the West Coast of our good old Oosa (GMT-8).

Q: Can I join Metanet?

A: There's a thread on the forum members' personal pictures here Go judge for yourself!

Q: Why do M&R never seem to be online?
A: They've got games to program and levels to make, d00000d. Let's see you try making something as good as n.

Quote: TornadoTK
How do you guys get into doing this?
A: Simple. You just stick with an idea, learn what you need to learn, and adapt from there. It'll take some time, though, so be patient.

At what age?
A: Any age can really start making a game. It might take age to comprehend the concepts of making one, but you can start... whenever you feel like it.

Does it cost?
A: It depends on what you use to create the game, because the foundation is everything. As said before, Flash is expensive, but effective. There's always C++, or for starters, Game Maker. You can do it without any cost, but then again, you'll have to sacrifice more time or more quality.

Is it really, really worth it?
A: Freeware games (assuming you're making freeware) are never worth it if you're doing it for the money. If it's for the fans, you will get that feeling of pride when you release a game that people really dig.

#2449 1 2005-04-06T16:47:58Z Keron Cyst
Q: Hi, I
A: First comes first. Check out the Forum Rules.

Q: What's with all the strict Post Count-monitoring & shtuff like that?
A: Here, someone who has posted a lot shows that he has been here for a while and knows shtuff. Furthermore, spam sucks up unnecessary bandwidth from Forumer; we're getting it free, and we ought not to waste space in return. Finally, :spam: = just about everywhere in the Internet-world. Plus, it's because in some forums people are able to actually help the forum & community grow (which is why PC is enabled for all forums under the N category), but in others (like Messageboard Games) people just spam pointlessly.

Q: I've a suggestion for the forums.
A: Go ahead and post it in General\This Forum. We're always open to new ideas.

Q: Can I become a staff member?
A: Well, you'll need a significant Post Count, and those posts should have contributed to the forum/community, N, NUMA, or something regarding MetaNet in some positive way. Keep doing so, and you can go apply in that one pinned thread regarding staff apps. at the top of General\This Forum. Then we'll go review your history on the forums, and we'll see if you can't be promoted to moderatorship

Q: Who's in charge of the forums?
A: You can view all the forum staff here. Mare & Raigan founded MetaNet Software in March 2004. I suggested to them the creation of a forum the following month after immediately getting hooked on the game. Then, an awesome crew of over 10 other staff members slowly followed, along with the steady growth of the board, into what we have now.

Q: You don't seem as strict as I thought
A: Yeah, I like to believe none of us are tyrants (of course, that eventually becomes impossible). Ask something, and depending on what it is, it usually gets done.

Q: What are the user groups?
A: Les'see... there are the following:
Guests: technically a user group only because the system won't allow it for anything else, guests can view the majority of the board but only post and start threads in a few, and cannot attach any files. Register, man!
Validating: this is the user group you're thrown into if you decide to register, or if you're changing your e-mail. You get a few more benefits than Guests, but only in completing e-mail validation can you rise to the generic Members base.
Members: that's the group you, if not currently are, used to be in. You get all the basic privileges a member has at most decent forums (hehe, decent indeed), including being able to see all the appropriate sub-bodies (except for maybe a couple, e.g. a Mod / Admin Discussion forum and a Bin for holding boring archives, but really minor ones), file-attaching to posts, etc.
Metanembers: Metanet + Members = Metanembers! Members must be handpicked to be promoted to Metanembership. They get a few benefits for having stuck around with the community for a while: max. upload file size is 750 instead of 500 KB; are allowed 12 e-mails per 12 hour period and one e-mail instead of 10, and 1 e-mail per 10 min. instead of 15 min.; max. PMs is 150 instead of 100; and probably some other tidbits I've forgotten. Ooh, did I mention being able to edit this very FAQ? But we'll be monitoring your actions, tho'! Abuse that ability and say good-bye to the class.
Privileged Mods: Thus far, Red Reamer is a privileged mod, purely for assisting me with physics homework in IRC. He governs T&I and can lock/open/split/merge/move topics, and edit/delete posts there. He also gets a few random benefits (slightly greater filesize, more PM storage capacity, etc. The same as Metanembership). Privileged moderators' abilities are restricted to only one or a few certain forums given when promoted to the new class (who monitors what forum should show underneath the forum's name).
Moderators: moderators can perform all actions which Privileged Mods can do, as well as remove posting rights temporarily/infinitely, warn/unwarn people, edit topic titles & descriptions, et cetera, et cetera, et cetera, throughout every forum section, and basically monitor the messageboard and make sure stuff doesn't get out of control. They can also edit your signature if it's unnecessarily large and remove your avatar if it's too obscene. Mods can do all sorts of stuff throughout the board Ph34r them! George, Obby, Tsukatu, and blue_tetris are all Moderators, for example.
Global Moderators: Basically, G-Mods have even more statistical advantages over all the other groups. (the creators of Metanet Software), and Kablizzy (one of the many leaders of Heroes of Ivalice, a forum-integrated RPGreferred to as HoI) occupies the Admin group.
Admin: Mare, Raigan, and I are the admins of this place, although M&R rarely come on once a month to post updates of any various events in their busy programming lives Admins can pre-register members, suspend/ban/unsuspend/unban members (also banning particular IPs for those jerks who just won't stop), change Member Titles, manually edit your Post Counts, etc.
Banned: The connection is simply refused. You can't view anything, and the page keeps showing something like "You have been banned from this forum!"
Others: there are a few user group oddballs out. That includes but is not limited to Daddaluma's personal FF6 Miniboss user group ("Daddaluma" is the name of a miniboss you encounter in Final Fantasy VI) who received it purely because he's 1337 like that, and because he's one of the oldest members on the board; the Legacy Elite, who can post in closed topics and get their own teal Online List color because they beat one or both of the staff-created Legacy levelpacks; and Purgatory, for those who simply can't behave (PM box is limited to something like 10 measly messages, they can't change their profiles, avatars, or signatures, etc. For the really unruly people ).
Tetrises from Around the World: Please don't ask. Kablizzy seems to have indulged in some sort of sickening request of blue_tetris (they are all alternative accounts for him)... Don't get any ideas, now. We very rarely allow multi-accounting at this place.

Oh, and almost every user group gives a unique color for members in them.

Q: Hey, who's "Administrator Bot?"
A: Administrator Bot (another account under the Admin user group) is just a universal admin account all the administrators have access to, for security purposes.

Q: "Member Titles?" What's a Member Title?
A: You see how you started off with "Newbie," then progressed to "Member" with Post Count, and so on and so forth? That's the forum's default Member Title system. I can manually change it to stick to something else permanently. Check out how wilderness's letting off the happiness, Tsukatu's a Grand Exalted B&T Overlord, etc.

Q: Cool. How can I get one?
A: We don't just hand Member Titles out like free passes to an amusement park (I used to, but that was when I was a moron, back in the day ). One of these two must occur, two of them unfortunately on your part:
  1. You must have done something very drastic in the community that affected numerous members (this can be a good or bad thing), like piss off a lot of people without actually breaking any forum rules, win a NTTS round or some other major contest, etc.
  2. You must be ber-1337 in some field, like working wonders with Paint, being a math genius, or helping Keron Cyst with his homework in the IRC room!
  3. (this counts as a third but it's so rare that I didn't label it above) An admin can give one at random to a member, whether he wants it or not. Heheh, that's always fun.
  4. You must have been around awhile. Members who have been here for years and have been contributive to the community are often rewarded with a Member Title, even if they haven't done anything revolutionary.
But at any given time you can lose your title or it can be replaced with something else, so don't take it for granted!

Q: You said something about warning above - how does the Warn System work?
A: A mod can warn you + or - 20% depending on something bad you've done; the mod can send you a PM or e-mail about why you were warned. If you made one, warn logs hamper your staff application severely when we look through your forum history to determine moderatorship, and basically tell you when to stop acting like a moron 100% gets you a forum suspension, so you don't want to go there!

Q: If you're suspended because of warns, how do you regress?
A: According to the Forum Rules, we'll keep the warn level at 100% for a month. Then we drop the warn % down by 20. One wrong move can get you back in Suspension Land, and can last from twice as long as that to a permanent ban, depending on the severity of the forum violation

Q: I was warned for "trolling." Whazzat?
A:
Quote: Wikipedia's article on Internet Trolls
A troll is someone who comes into [a] forum, and posts inflammatory, rude or offensive messages designed to annoy and antagonize the existing members or disrupt the flow of discussion.

Q: Those Google ads at the top are annoying.
A: If you're running the Mozilla Firefox browser you can download an extension called Adblock which allows you to completely remove it via right-click and a bit of fiddling! Eh, as for the non-Windows users... it probably won't be too hard to find a similar app. for your OS

Q: I want a sig that lets me click it to reveal more, but it doesn't work. HELP!
A: Surprisingly enough, they do work. When you update your signature with spoiler tags, the preview window makes it seem that it isn't working, but it is. So if you put the code in, check another thread that you posted in. If it's working in there, it's fine; if not, consult a more BBCode-fluent member via PM for assistance in getting it to work.[/color]

Q: Can you edit the FAQs?
A: Thats one of those super-cool things only metanembers get to do! (Oh, and the higher ranking officials)!

Q: What are the gold blocks for? When do I get another level?
A: Each gold block represents a Member title, each new title is achieved by a new gold 'pip', which are achieved by post count, this doesn't mean that you spam across the board, if you are found doing so, your post count will be reduced, some people have minus post count because of moderators having a little 'fun'. Find the complete list here.[/color]

Q: I just got told I revived a thread. What's that?
A: Reviving a thread is when someone posts in a thread over around 2 months old. This means that the topic is dead and no longer a point of interest.[/color] Reviving is rarely a problem when you've got something meaningful to contribute to the topic at hand. Posting something like "thats cool " is not a useful contribution and we don't like seeing it. Apart from looking at dates, you can be pretty certain that topics on the first page of a subforum are active and popular.

Q: The forums are moving? lol wut?!
A:[/color]Yes, believe it or not the forums are moving to http://forum.therealn.com/ You should make an account there in the same name as your account here. More information can be found in the pinned news article.

Q: How can I help stop the redundancy of asking a question that's already been asked or suggesting a suggestion that's already been suggested?
A: 'Tis quite simple: use the engine at the top of the forums, and try to find any posts that relate to your problem or concern. Enter keywords for what it is you're looking for. If you don't find it on the first try, don't give up; try more times with different search terms. If you still can't find what you're looking for, then feel free to post away! (and make sure you say that you couldn't find it so you don't get flamed by jerks here)
- - - - - - - - - -
Q: What is "1337 / g33k-t4lk?" I hear about it so often on the Internet
A: G33k-T4lk is a kind of Internet-language used by nerds, script kiddies (simple virus programmers), etc. It regards using any symbols except actual letters to resemble letters. Some are static (there's only one way to resemble it), but it really depends on the person. In G33k-T4lk, "1337" = "leet" = "elite," although most say those who speak in G33k-T4lk are morons who have no life
Here are some inflexible, always-the-same translations:

E = 3 (I don't know anyone who has E for something other than 3; maybe the Euro sign)
D = Almost always |); can be [), etc.
H = |-|
P = Almost always either |> or |*
R = |2 (if you slightly bent the 2 diagonally, it looks like the right side of an R)
S = 5
And so on. It really depends on you; letter symbols are really flexible if you can picture it right (e.g. A = 4 or /-\).

In "minor g33k-t4lk" - as the above is totally hardcore - only a few replacement symbols are used, like "t3h" = "the," & "j00" = "you." For some reason j is pronounced as a y I don't see why, because a Y is just as easily put into symbolization: `/.

Example text:
1 |200|_ _|00! = I rool joo! = I rule you!

You can find the Wikipedia's extensive information and history on Leet here.

/\/0V\/, |_37'5 533 1|= _|00 (4/V |)3(1|>|-|3|2 7|-|15!

Q: Why do karate people grunt when they punch/kick?
A: (Thanks to ShadyTrader for this bit of info) Well, yelling might demoralize the enemy or make bystanders think you're crazy and flee, and it tightens your abs and other torso muscles so hits to your chest or stomach wouldn't hurt as bad Plus (this, thanks to wilderness), as you attack, your body tenses, and on impact, you release it. The exulsion of air increases your focus and adds weight to your thrust, kick, jab etc. Furthermore, (epigone edit) the 'grunt' being referred to here is actually called a kiai (pronounced key-eye), which is a Japanese word that roughly translates to 'spirit yell.' The idea is to internally focus your energy and release it in one explosive force of will. Want to know more?

Q: How do I take screenshots?
A: On Windows, press the Print Screen button - located above Insert in most keyboards - to copy a capture of your screen to your computer's clipboard. Alternatively, Alt + Print Screen takes a capture of your currently selected window. Then, open any image editor (even Paint will do), and paste the capture with Ctrl + V. Remember to save the result and you're done.

Q: I want to add something to these FAQs.
A: Feel free to PM any of the Metanembers; go to one's profile page and click "Personal Message" on the right.

Quote: Moment Piece
I looked behind myself for a mement, only to see the two snarling figures hot on my trail. All I could make out were their metallic-blue eyes peering through the bare, snow-dusted trees. How strange it was that those two things so evil could come from such beauty as the forest. The contrast was intriguing, and I almost stopped running just to stare. The two beasts gained on me, and the beads of eyes started to become much, much bigger. I could now make out their figures and learned that they weren't ugly at all. In fact, they were devilishly beautiful.
They were two hybrid creatures, a mixture of what seemed to be a wolf and a stag. Their bodies were furry and slender, and they were quite agile; they were perfectly shaped and trained machines to attack. Their very thick legs came out of their body very thick and widely, with obviously distinguished muscles, and were quite long, and as your eyes traveled to the foot, you would see the leg becoming thinner and thinner, finally expanding for the hoof. Their necks were very thick, a combination of the hair's fluffiness, and the extremely solid muscles to hold their long antlers up. As they ran, their fur was pushed back and rippled by the wind, creating an arrow-like effect. But the features that stood out the most were their eyes. They were as azure as the sky, and if you looked straight into them, you could feel them peering into your soul, evaluating and judging you, bit by bit. And they were vibrant.
As I ran, I started to tire out. I was running barefoot and almost naked, and both the brambles and twigs on the ground and the cold wind cut into my skin and caused extreme pain. I leaned over and picked up some bark from the ground and attempted to cover myself. I shivered and breathed a white puff of breath. As it rose through the atmosphere it was like an angel ascending to heaven. Finally it expanded and dissappeared, and my visualization was lost. My hope was lost. I had no more strength, and couldn't go on. The beasts could do their worst ton me, no matter the pain. I would leave this life of misery and grief, and face the unknown.
I looked at the ground rushing by me and tried to time my fall. I was already in so much pain, and I knew that if I didn't fall safely, I would probably die. I looked ahead of me, and saw a pile of snow near a tree. I didn't think; I didn't want to think. I closed my eyes and jumped.
I didn't even feel the impact. I just felt the cold snow rub against my open wounds. I didn't care. I would let them do their worst. I was limp, and could barely see anything but two blurry figures approaching rapidly, and I didn't care. I would let them do their worst. They slowed down, and cautiously padded up. They reeked of excrement. I didn't care. I would let them do their worst. They poked at me with their snouts, and pawed at my arms with their hoofs, making sure I wasn't a threat. I didn't care. Their hoofs were surprisingly warm and smooth; perfect blunt weapons. I would let them do their worst. They both looked at me in the eye, and that was the last thing I saw. I didn't care. I would let them do their worst.
I was blind now - I had to rely only on my ears to know what they were doing to me, for now my body was entirely numb. My arms and legs were probably broken, or at least sprained. Something cool and wet brushed against my leg. One of the animals was licking my leg clean. The other was brushing the snow off me with his antlers. I felt relaxed; I felt ready. As one of them fitted its teeth around my legs, I smiled, and almost laughed. To die would really be a great adventure.
My right leg was gone. I couldn't feel it anymore, and certainly couldn't move it. It was the only part of my body that was in extreme pain. I felt the ground with my hands, brushing against one of the creatures' feet. I quickly pulled away, and kept feeling around. Right next to me was a tree stump, and I leaned my head back to rest on it. I wasn't in any pain anymore now - I could just feel the blood clinging to my skin. As my blind eyes faced the sky, I started to see something. I saw darkness. Utter and complete darkness. And as the two monsters ripped at my flesh, the darkness was ripped away by little spots of light, as if somebody was sticking twigs through a dark sheet of cloth one by one. Slowly, a little white spot appeared in the middle of my line of vision, and started to grow so subtly and slowly that it was unseeable.
The dot grew bigger and bigger, and became a star, then an eye, then the moon, and then the sun. I could feel my body getting lighter. My torso had less and less to support. The little dot of light had become enormous, and was filling my whole view. My legs started to get warm, and the sensation traveled up my body until it reached my head. I felt quite comfortable. All of a sudden the nice warmth shot away and was soon replaced by a chilling trickle down my spin. I shuddered at the iciness, and started to quietly moan. It became louder, and evolved into a scream. I was screaming at the top of my lungs. I screamed for what seemed like hours, but was probably seconds. Finally, I lost energy amnd collapsed. I stopped screaming. I stopped hurting. I stopped being cold. I stopped being. I stopped.
I wasn't alive when the beasts were done with me, but I could still hear them softly. They growled at each other and howled in unison as I drifted off to a better place.
...
Some of those marks are from my personal opinion (a.k.a. optional).

Quote: readme_e.TXT
* How to play

Steer a boat and sink enemy fleet.

- Controls

o Move
Arrow / Num / [WASD] / [IJKL]  / Joystick

Main Title & Automatic Fire:


Quote: readme_e.TXT
o Fire guns / Hold direction
[Z][L-Ctrl][R-Ctrl][.]        / Trigger 1, 4, 5, 8

Hold a key to open automatic fire and hold the direction of a boat.
Tap a key to take a turn while firing.

o Fire lance
[X][L-Alt][R-Alt][L-Shift][R-Shift][/][Return] / Trigger 2, 3, 6, 7

Lance is a single-shot weapon. You have to tap a key to fire a next lance.
You can't fire a next lance while a first lance is in a screen.

Lance:


Quote: readme_e.TXT
- Rank multiplier

Rank multiplier (displayed in the upper right) is a bonus multiplier
that increases with a difficulty of a game.
You can increase a rank multiplier faster by going forward faster.

- Boss appearance timer

Boss appearance timer (displayed in the upper left) is a remaining time
before a boss ship appears.

Apparently when you die you respawn with an octagonal shield alongside your temporary invincibility that can protect you from one shot. Use it wisely



Look at the trapped boat to the right Green is land. Some shallow ground blocks only movement, but not projectiles. There are turrets mounted on some land.



Red lines converging upon you show where enemies are located. If the space between two lines is filled, that shows that the enemy is using a heavy weapon which covers over a lot of space.


All the enemies have a red core. You can destroy their turrets, but the gunboat's mainframe doesn't go down until you destroy their central core. This applies to bosses as well, so make sure when you encounter bosses their core's in view, as the screen doesn't move upwards when you're fighting one.


Don't know how to get past bosses? Stick this file in Gunroar\replay, watch the replay in the main menu, and observe how I do it You can easily bypass bosses, but you don't get any points for it.

Quote: Tsukatu, 2005-06-27T10:45:10Z
... make it so that the end of your sentence fills their head with simultaneous thoughts, most of which will induce some kind of panic or hesitation individually.... let's say you're having a casual talk with a friend of yours and out of nowhere he starts lying to you about something. It would be stupid to try to cleverly trap him by proving that parts of his story couldn't work out, because that will make him focus primarily on inventing a story even though it will make him start to panic a little. A better way would be to keep looking straight into his eyes as you pause after hearing his response, then say something like, "alright, I'm going to ask you again, and this time I'd appreciate it if you didn't lie to me. What blah blah blah?" Yes, it does sound like you're interrogating them, but think of it this way - if you were in that position and you told what you thought was a convenient lie and he starts slowly doubting you, you could manage to uphold the story by adding things and leaving things ambiguous, etc.; but if you were asked politely to stop lying, you'd turn red instantly, and you'll receive all sorts of lingering and panic-inducing thoughts like, "oh shit, he knows I'm lying," "for future reference, it's a bad idea to lie to this guy," "I don't want him to get angry at me," "I hope he's not angry right now," and "I wasn't very nice to lie to him, was I?" All sorts of these will strike all at the same time, and the first words out of your mouth if you're hit with that rush of panic will be something like "uhhh... um.... uh..." And think about it - you'd consider that person influential and intelligent, and it'd feel more like you have to earn his respect (which people constantly strive for)....

One-minute Drawing Contest

Use Paint and any of its sidebar tools (or any simple drawing app. if you're a non-Windows user) to quickly whip up an image in one minute or less; watch the corner computer clock, and stick it in an attachment to a reply in this thread!

Rules:
1. Don't cheat and go over the time. It might be worth the risk, but if too many people get suspicious and
2. Only a simple utility; e.g. not Photo Shop No special effects. If another person can't recreate a similar copy in less than 10 minutes, then it'll probably be frowned upon.
3. Draw it from scratch. No inspiration whatsoever (or an old image that you're adding to); just get a blank, white flat screen and start doodling.
4. Only one entry. You can keep scrapping and restarting a pic. as many times as you want, tho'
5. It can be about anything legal!! Draw a pic. of bullets ricocheting off of walls, your favorite car, a, uh, dgh... plane, yourself, whatever!

Judges! I'm not picking out the finalists (just two phases) on my own You cannot judge if you're competing.



Now get drawing!

Quote: The URL above
Category: Strategy
Players: To be determined
Release Date: Sep 19, 2005
 Publisher: Nintendo




Battalion Wars blazes onto Nintendo GameCube with a platoon of real-time strategy (RTS) action. Whether players are hoofing it across the plains as a lone infantryman or commanding an entire platoon from atop an armored tank, the challenge is real and the mission is critical. There has never been a real-time strategy title like this before.

Command forces in the heat of battle, but beware. Clever enemy AI will adapt to every move.

Hop behind the wheel of multiple attack vehicles: Pilot jeeps, tanks, helicopters, airborne gunships, fighter jets, transport vehicles and more.

Take the fight to foes with a massive arsenal of weapons such as rifles, bazookas, flamethrowers, machine guns, mortars, rocket launchers and many others.

Countries will rise or fall based on players tactics, and guiding troops has never been easier. Want to station forces on a ridge? Send a scout team to spy on the enemy? Charge headlong into the breach? Battalion Wars lets players do it all at the touch of a button.

Storyline

Dark days are rising at the end of the 21st century. What started as a border spat between the Western Frontier and the Tundran Territories has snowballed into a terrifying global conflict one in which the armies have fought each other to a standstill. As their once-proud forces limp through the seemingly endless war, a despotic madman, Kaiser Vlad, seeks to take advantage of the stalemate and seize control of both nations.

The Kaiser is the former leader of Xylvania, which was annexed by the Western Frontier and Tundran Territories during their war. Deprived of his armies and thirsty for revenge, Vlad uses secret offshore accounts and unholy science to create a terrible army of super powerful, gas-breathing, Chemical Shock Troops.

When Vlad unleashes the warriors, it takes both superpowers by surprise. Weakened by their prolonged conflict and seemingly helpless against this new threat, the Frontier and Tundran armies form a desperate alliance in an attempt to repel the Kaiser. Can this new coalition use pluck and guile to overcome the forces of darkness, or will both nations fall under the boot heel of a madman?

Characters

The player-controlled Western Frontier forces are lead by General Herman and Colonel Austin. They are joined by Betty, who gives mission briefings, objective updates and helpful intel.

The Tundran army is commanded by Tzar Gorgi and Marshal Nova. Once bitter enemies of the Western Frontier, they have put aside old feelings to combat the Xylvanian menace.

The nefarious Xylvanian forces are lead by they power-hungry Kaiser Vlad. His right hand is the beautiful and deadly Countess Ingrid.

How to Progress through the Game

Battalion Wars contains more than 20 unique missions, each with a number of sub-quests and goals. Once in a mission, players can complete it any way they choose. Need to blow up a tank? Go the stealthy route and send a squad through the forest to ambush it from behind, or just hop into a tank and charge! Real-time strategy meets full-on action.

Special Features

Most PC-based real-time strategy games have complicated controls, and translating them to consoles can be a challenge. Battalion Wars does a masterful job of making it simple, yet effective. A single button press summons troops, while a second sends them off to fight. Posting sentries, driving vehicles and accessing the all-important battlefield map is easy and intuitive.

Direct link to image gallery

Franz Liszt's Friska is making me talk to myself while I practice it, saying "No, 4... not 5, 4" (fingering; 1 = thumb, 5 = fifth finger, etc.), and "Oh, my gosh; the first part was already hard! Why'd he have to make a variation out of it?!" If you've ever heard the last half of Tom's piano music as he performs for a huge audience in a great concert in Quinton's Tom & Jerry cartoon, The Cat Concerto, that's part of Friska (Quinton -- producer of Tom & Jerry (on cable TV) -- combined Liszt's Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2 and that). I think it starts somewhere on the first or second page of the song when the hammers wake up Jerry, who's sleeping inside the piano.

If you don't quite remember it, all I can tell you is that it's where Tom's pinky on his right hand has to stretch almost a foot to nail a key that is played every two notes while the thumb & index (I think middle, maybe) play the melody; you encounter that section ~3-4 times throughout the piece. And it goes insanely fast.

#4692 1 2005-10-10T01:12:24Z Keron Cyst
Quote
Schwarzenegger signs game-restriction bill

Measure won't become California law until January, but the ESA is already planning a suit.

One was a Democratic Chinese-American child psychologist and anti-media-violence advocate representing San Francisco's sleepy Sunset district. The other was a Republican Austrian bodybuilder who became governor after making millions starring in violent Hollywood blockbusters. But today, Assemblyman Leland Yee and Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger found common ground over one subject: video games.

This afternoon, Schwarzenegger signed California bill AB1179, which Yee penned, into law. The bill, which will come into effect January 1, 2006, bans the sale or rental of "violent video games" to children. What exactly is a "violent video game"? According to the state's legal summary of the bill, a "violent" game is defined as a "game in which the range of options available to a player includes killing, maiming, dismembering, or sexually assaulting an image of a human being." That definition would seem to cover virtually every M-for-Mature-rated game and many T-for-Teen rated games as well.

Under the new law, retailers that sell such games would be subject to a $1,000 fine. It will also require "violent" video games to bear a two-inch-by-two-inch sticker with a "solid white '18' outlined in black" on their front covers. That's over twice the size of the labels that currently adorn game-box covers and display the familiar Entertainment Software Ratings Board (ESRB) rating.

Given Schwarzenegger's close ties to the entertainment industry, it must have been a difficult choice to sign the bill. However, the governor played up the decision as a proactive move to shield youngsters from harmful material. "This gets the parents involved in the decision-making process," he said in a statement. "I believe as an actor in the ratings system. It is very important to protect children."

The Entertainment Software Association (ESA), the top US game industry lobby and parent of the ESRB, was quick to respond. "We are disappointed that politicians of both parties chose to toss overboard the First Amendment and free artistic and creative expression in favor of political expediency," said ESA president Doug Lowenstein in an statement. "AB 1179 is punitive against retailers, will waste limited taxpayer dollars, and when it is struck down by the courts, as has been the fate of similar statutes, parents will be no better off for this effort to damage one of the state's fastest growing and most exciting industries that is providing some of the most compelling entertainment in the world today." Lowenstein said the ESA is already planning a lawsuit to have the bill deemed unconstitutional.

California is the latest state to restrict the sales of video games. It follows Michigan and Illinois, both of which passed measures restricting the sale of violent or sexually explicit games. Oklahoma and Mississippi are considering similar measures.

By Tor Thorsen -- GameSpot
Posted Oct 7, 2005 4:13 pm PT

I don't think it'll bother me at all. I may be a fan of Nintendo but I could live easily without it; in fact I haven't touched any console other than the PC for months now. Soldat is all me, man

But I don't think a law is needed for that; parents should have the final say.

November 19, at around brunch time (GMT-8):
1. I go check the MN forums
2. I fail to log in. I retry twice, actually watching my fingers the other times It still fails.
3. I scroll to the top of the board and see that the top category has changed from "N" to "Chonnymon is a GOD Hacker"
4. I look at the Online List and see Keron Cyst viewing a member's profile when it should say Keron Cyst is viewing the Online List
5. I post that vulgar thread in the B&T urgently telling Kablizzy to reset my password, without realizing that Kablizzy's account has already been deleted, along with the other admins'
6. I hold an AIM instant message with 7654321 as I helplessly hit F5 in horror, slowly watching all the forum names change into random junk
7. I sulk on not having set LV to admin already, and then after the FAQ has changed to "ITEK Help" and the forum below it has changed, the category changes to something like "I feel guilty" (I don't remember exactly)
8. "NO worryies your pass and usernames hav been restord"
9. I try to log in, but it fails. I log in again 2 min. later and it works
10. I immediately check the admin log for the foreign IP Keron Cyst was using and ban it, and start reverting the names of the forums
11. I get a PM from ITEK saying that he's sorry he kind of went overboard but was simply telling me that my password of 6 #s is really too simple and that I ought to make it more complex
12. Right at the moment Chonnymon sends an IM through AIM to me, sending me URLs of the hash-searching site he used to look up my password and a database of collected exploits of various websites (which I'll be checking later to guard this forum against any other possible hacks), and also tells that lowercase and uppercase letters confuse the hash-searcher heavily; I thus unban him so he can read my notes to him in the forum (the first digits of his IP were 170-172; I forgot exactly what, but I can look it up again)
12½. He says that ITEK assisted him with the hacking and also persuaded him to give me back my password
13. Everyone overreacts (that was fun)
14. I reregister the deleted admin trio back in after e-mailing them all
15. Later that night Kablizzy posts his leave without even reading any further into the event than "1337 h4x" and uses his admin account to delete himself
16. I change my password at the MN forums and my e-mail account after typing up some 1337-sp34k in Notepad and copying it and pasting it into the respective password bars. I essentially locked myself out of my Yahoo! account (for some reason it keep sayng it's invalid) and lost a ton of information, and have now reverted to my emergency Gmail account until I can contact Yahoo! Customer Care (I'm pathetic)

November 21 (today), at 9:00 in the morning (GMT-8):
1. I go on my ME to check if the Soldat forums are still down
2. I see the board with a red, changed skin (one of the many precustomized skins Forumer has) and think Wow, Mare's sure been busy.

4. I log in this time but see that I am now a Global Moderator
5. I get PMs; some say "WTF is going on[/i]" mainly, "If you're the hacker you're gh3y" (heh), and "Are you able to do anything about it? Is there anything I can do to help?"
6. I see a thread under News saying "Do you want your forum back?" by administrator Lavary
7. I post in it, thinking it might be possible to reach the thousand posts if his GMT is not +2 (he demanded there must be 1000 posts by 10 PM), skimming over the fact that he said they must be all from different members
8. I go on Gaim and miraculously find Chonnymon online
9. I ask him to hack into his account and restore me to admin status (if he hacked into mine there's no point since a Global Mod can't promote himself to admin)
10. He says his password was "lavary"
11. I immediately suspend admin Lavary for 365 days, then ban his IP, and then delete his account
12. I try to tend with the chaos, and revert the skin back to regular IPB (darn it, those custom images took a while to load into the system )
13. Out of ph34r of t3h 1337 h4x0r possibly having a dynamic IP I immediately head back to the Ban Settings and stick wildcards on his IP and other adjacent IPs



14. Chonnymon's IP was also close to his. In banning those IPs and labeling wildcards he is also banned from the forums, so if another hacker comes by he won't be able to help.



I am creating a new security measure as you read this.

#5876 1 2005-12-24T21:02:20Z Keron Cyst
Metal Arms: Glitch in the System is one of the hardest console games I've ever played. I'm only on I think level 16 or 17 (right after you work with Krunk and his Control Tether) out of 42. And this is just on Normal. I simply must try Nuts of Steel afterwards (last difficulty, after Hard)

It steals so much from Halo; the tanks are Scorpions (they both have m. guns and turrets), the gun turrets are Shades, the enemies consist of specific classes with types distinguished by color, Grunts are Grunts (both panic if in small numbers), RATs are like Warthogs (driver, and independent gunner in the back)... xD Plus you have a Primary and Secondary weapon, which you scroll through columns of boxes on either side of the screen by holding a key and using L & R, with which you can also view data on a weapon (MGS! ).

But it also has 1337 physics, and the AI is one of the best I've seen. The enemies actually throw 'nades, take cover, and jump from ledge to ledge! The graphics are also beautiful, if you've seen screenies of it. IMO best game of '03.

Romans 12: 16-18 (NIV), verse superscripts excluded
Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but be willing to associate with people of low position. Do not be conceited. Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Be careful to do what is right in the eyes of everybody. If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.

... then it goes on saying that God will avenge you after death, but that doesn't really apply here as actions have to be taken while we're still alive to keep this board running

I don't think I behave conceitedly (for those who say "Well, you made this thread," this is of course in response to those who think I'm a bad admin ) - I'm sometimes actually a bit ashamed of how I behave as according to admins on other boards, who tend to be "professional," hardly appearing, fear-striking into the hearts of newbies when they ban someone, never making any personal connections to plain members and only speaking to the staff strictly about forum business (and yes, I am aware that a bit of MetaNet's philosophy is that being criticized for being unprofessional is considered a compliment to them). I'm as active as a moderator and I post public polls and such to kind of follow Ho Chi Minh in that we both get down to the common people's level and gather support from there. Inquiry threads regarding feedback directly to this board can be read by and actually heeded by the greatest power (here, admins) and bring more incentive to staying (which is probably why we have such a large community).

Point is, that's why I'm so slow to anger and to penalize anyone; I don't think I've warned anyone for months now, and people think I'm retarded for that. I try to analyze every situation before making an extreme move - unless the offender did something totally inexcusable, like posting a virus or such - and am very lenient towards others (the 1LoG is a direct example of that), which is probably why the forums have so much activity (people are able to receive more personalization than most other boards and their suggestions are considered, and thus stick around for being recognized more than most forums).
So if you think I act really immature, it's indeed true in a sense. But there's more than meets the eye to not just myself but quite most of our people here

Quote: Chain e-mail I received; BBCode added
NEW YORK Friday may be D-day, as in "destruction day," for millions of Windows computer users.

That's the day a notably pesky e-mail worm, variously called "Nyxem.E," "CME-24," "BlackWorm," "Mywife.E," "KamaSutra" and "VB.bi," among other names, is set to detonate its deadly payload.

Once activated, the worm will corrupt all documents on a infected machine with the following file extensions: .dmp, .doc, .mdb, .mde, .pdf, .psd, .ppt, .pps, .rar, .xls and .zip.

That means almost all files created using Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel or Microsoft PowerPoint could be lost forever, as well as "raw" Adobe Photoshop files, PDF files used by Adobe Acrobat and competing PDF readers, and several kinds of database and compression files.

Hundreds of thousands of Windows machines are believed to have already been infected, mostly in India, Peru, Turkey and Italy, said Mikko Hypponen, chief research officer for Finnish security company F-Secure Corp.

The worm also tries to disable anti-virus software that is out of date, Hypponen said. Thus, users should make sure their software is turned on and has the latest definitions, generally available for free from the software vendor's Web site.

F-Secure also has created free removal tools for two different versions of the worm, available here and here.

"If you are infected, and you find out about it today, you still have time to get rid of the virus," Hypponen said.

Nyxem.E hasn't spread as far or as fast as many recent e-mail worms. But worms these days are generally meant to help spammers and hackers carry out attacks, not destroy files, so the impact this time may be more severe.

Microsoft Corp. issued an advisory Tuesday warning customers about the worm, which affects most versions of Windows.

Users should be safe if they have the latest anti-virus software or if their computers are set with limited privileges, a common setting in larger organizations.

They are vulnerable if they, like many small business and home users, leave their computers set with full administrative rights.

Users should also check the date on the computer. The worm hits the third of every month, so if the computer's local calendar settings are off, Hypponen said, files may be destroyed sooner or later, even if the computer is never turned on Friday.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

S.W.I.N.E.
Developer: Stormregion
Publisher: Fishtank Interactive

On August 3, under the orders of General Iron Tusk, the NATIONAL
ARMY OF PIGS crossed the border without warning and penetrated deep
into Carrotland territory. Within only two weeks, they'd burned
everything to the ground. The capital city is under blockade. As a
result of the bitter fighting, the rabbit army is decimated. Towns and
villages are deserted. The defense's determined efforts have not been
crowned by success, and their reduced army cannot stop the hordes of
swine. In desperation, the government and the staff of generals reach
the following decision: Because overwhelming Iron Tusk's war machine
with a frontal attack is impossible, we will have to resort to
subterfuge. From the remains of their reserves, the rabbits create a
powerful fighting force. Without suffering too many losses, this force
must harass and sneak attack the enemy until they lose all their
supply lines and military objectives. Now, all that remains is to find
a capable officer who can lead this operation...

Originally a commercial game Stormregion released S.W.I.N.E.
for freeware just last Christmas. Downloads from servers since have
picked up to over 100,000 counts.
"Don't be a Carrotland-rabbit, download and play: the National Pig
Army authorized the free usage of this software."

EDIT I'm gonna kill the quote that the below passage should normally have; I've edited too much already for it to be truly authentic anymore.


=-=-=-=-=-=


A weird Californian, Internet alias being "Keron Cyst," found N on GameHippo and out of the blue from seemingly instant addiction suggested in May 2004 to Mare Sheppard that a messageboard ought to be created to bind a potential community that it may have gathered.

Plans were set, a .TXT blueprint of the generic categories, forums, and child forums of the messageboard was concocted, and an IPB board hosted by Forumer under the name "metanet" on server 2 was created purely because Cyst's previous obsession with the WhiteSpace Unlimited community (creators of the Stick Soldiers series) bore forums under Forumer, which was quite new at the time.

[ Yet somehow MN was able to establish a forum on server 2 (hence metanet.2.forumer.com) while the old SS forums were located on server 4 ]

(The newest SS forum is now hosted by Andrew Russell Studiosthe people behind SS3and is powered by SMF, not IPB.)

Ironically, Cyst was too busy with the basic forum setup at the time to worry about new staff (the forums were very small back then, anyways), and didn't help M&R with handpicking any potential moderators; in fact, he didn't even know any of their personal contributions and personalities, but seeing how the duo were smart enough to make N ( ) he went forward with the new staff member selections (Kablizzy, maximo, and LittleViking001) without hesitation as minor Moderators of the forum. Two are now Administrators and one is a Global Moderator.

Tsukatu came along later, a bit shortly after the Bash & Thrash forum was created, and what with his blatant swearing and criticisms of people's maps was unanimously elected for B&T Tyrant. He is now retired and iangb has taken his place as Sukian in his popular pinned thread at the top of the B&T.

Mojo's banner was thrown at the top of the boards (I think you can still find my test thread about it on one of the last pages of Tests & Inquiries somewhere) after showing off his Photoshop expertise and making sig. images for numerous people.

Some time between Kablizzy joining the forums and December 2004, The Wunder Bunny conspired with Cyst for a 2005 forum surprise, which was specifically the revamp in the Forumer skin (that is, making many images N-friendly). He was supposedly suspended (until Jan. 15, I recall ) because Cyst had told him of what he was going to do to the forum skin and Kablizzy wanted to tell some others (I actually seriously thought of kicking him out of the boards temporarily because of that possibility, which was where the conspiracy sparked from), and he supposedly went on a mass swearing spree, PMing Cyst rather vulgar remarks about his belief in strict constitution (I actually favor loose, but that was the way I was thinking at the time ), which gave him public evidence to boot him. The event was dubbed the Kablizzy Fiasco alongside the 2005 Forum Surprise.

[ Ironically, Cyst actually did suspend Kablizzy for a day, just so he could see what the board looked like when one was rejected by its system ]

I think a bit after the beginning of the year 2005, Arachnid made an IRC room from irc.mware.ca for the community and "moderates" NUMA Discussion (being its webmaster).

The Youth & Beauty Brigade, a large trivia search by the staff, also occurred. This made use of the password-protected forum icon, a Floorchaser. A bit after the Y&BB completed (or collapsed? hm), a password-protected forum was created for Trogdor007 and some others in a futile attempt to revive another puzzler for the community. It died before it was born.

nevermore, Maniac, and tktktk (I think iangb was a bit earlier) all were promoted simultaneously as a result of the need for more staff members of the growing messageboard, which then had ~1500 users.

Cyst then made the FAQs, finally finding a use for his read-only forum icon.

sweep becoming a mod was one of the more recent actions, after the post-Thanksgiving November hacking attacks (you can find synopses on those in the N Wikicities, which have a link at the bottom of the board index).

blue_tetris has also become a regular Moderator, away from RPG Moderator status like Daddaluma. sweep currently vies in competition against blue_tetris for control over forum subsections.


=-=-=-=-=-=
