The problem is that this doll analogy is too static, restricting the entire system into only considering those dolls (or even the one "misbehaving" doll) alone. If God tortured one person who He made into existence and crafted into whatever that person behaved like, then yeah, He might be considered horrific. (Actually, not evenand this ties into maestro's protest, but let me get to that in a bit.) But suppose the dolls are animated and put into a society. And they influence each other. Just to keep things simple, we'll say that knocking over a teacup sends a doll to... uh... a pile of firewood, and setting a teacup back on a table (and this is a gigantic warehouse with numerous dolls, tables and one teacup for eachsymbolizing a doll's lifewe're talking about) brings the doll to... hm... let's say the room upstairs, to simulate heaven. The table denotes the holy path in life, and the dolls can... reproduce...



You know what? Your blasted analogy is wayyyyy too simple. No wonder it's easily perceived as the rot that anyone would shrink away in disgust from. Here, let me just address free will (since that's the concept it strikes at, no?) and see if I can just respond to God's atrociousness indirectly, because I really don't think I'll get very far being stuck with those doll...ies.


*** FREE WILL ALONGSIDE GOD'S OMNIPOTENCE

Now we come to free will's collision with God's omnisciencehow we can have free will if God has already set specific people for heaven and hell. If you want to take God out of the picture, you can call this determinism, or naturalism, or fate, or destinythe idea that, given the way the universe was structured and assembled at the beginning, Mare and Raigan were bound by nature and their past to program N and build Metanet, I was bound by my month-long addiction to N to create this board under Mare's supervision, we were bound to have this digital conversation.

(Let me just throw this in real quick, though it might be a bit off-topic: Paul explains that technically no one is free; everyone is either a slave to God or the devil. And for those who don't believe in them, the same concepts that they stand for can substitute. In their hearts when all veils are uncovered, everyone pursues either spiritual or material wealth. Anyways, to return...)

The stumbling block is this: determinists declare that you had no choice but to read this. You were ultimately, given the events of your past (which shaped your personality, beliefs, and ideals and gave you the physical, emotional, and mental stability you currently bear in you, your physical body), you "had no choice" but to ultimately come upon this thread, to somehow manage to find this section in this ridiculously gigantic post (I think probably the largest I've ever made in my life! Ha), and to reflect on this.

But think about this:

Aren't you willingly doing this? You are reading this because you want to, regardless of whether you are masochistically procrastinating or are just bored, or consider this a relevant, substantial issue to devote your time to; you're doing this of your own free will. (I was about to create a counterargument for myself and suggest that one of you has a boss who's demanding you to go to the Serious Discussion section of Metanet and debate philosophy or else he'd fire you, but...)

Here's an image that I like to portray: imagine that all the events in the universe are on the most gargantuan, sprawled-out timeline you could possibly be stepping on and reading, and we're standing on the section that says "People reading Topic #22606 of the http://metanet.x.am forum." Imagine that this is a giant scroll that God has, to monitor everything that has occurred and that will occur.

Now let's consider Him rolling up the scroll, or even destroying it completely.

Now does that suddenly alter what you were going to do? Not at all! (Haha, I'm talking like Paul now. He follows up questions with "Not at all!" all the time, esp. in Romans.) God's knowledge of your future doesn't suddenly limit your free will; you were still planning to read this even if God wasn't omniscient. And now let me go the naturalistic way for nonbelievers. Sure, you were destined by the raw structure of the neurons in your cortical regions, being established in those exact ways over the years and according to your parents' & ancestors' genes, and recent events since even yesterday, to lead you to pop onto Metanet and check out this topic. Then why do you not feel restrained? If you don't feel restrained in any way, why does iangb thus call it an "illusion"? What is "free"? So you had the choice of water or milk. If you chose water, who's to say that you were forced to take the water? You wanted to take the water.

Determinism says that you cannot possibly have taken the milkright! You never planned to take the milk anyways. There's no problem. You are passively (or actively, even) following determinism/fate/destiny whether you like it or not, and that's how they came to earn the terms... popularly fate or destiny. God or no God, free will fits perfectly with omniscience or determinism; we freely follow the sole path that it establishes. (Or youas I, probably just personally, docould merge both thoughts, and consider that God's omniscience is this knowledge, since the beginning everything we know, of how all these causes and effects will generate new causes and effects to ultimately achieve His Will.)

But since I'm arguing for the divine, I'll have to return to the topic at handthe nature of His Will, which would then cause you to say "But in that case, God is sending people to Hell while knowing it." (I earlier covered the shaky topic of those who have never been exposed to Christianity through God's specific control of people; the world and every single person, organism, and atom is progressing in the single best way possible, and if it was made any differentthat is, if Strife's Buddhist heard of Christianity, then there would be more who wouldn't in such an alternate time. So here I'll refer to those who have actively rejected it.) Such people might unfortunately even be you, a reader here. (And I truly do mean that unfortunately, if I don't seem like I do.) But now consider this; if that is true, then change.

You see? You don't want to change! Some of you don't even, based off of various posts, want to consider God (or for a few, even anything "illogical") at all. So whether God is omniscient or not, you're still deciding to take an escalator down to Hell of completely and solely of your own accord and doing.


*** GOD'S SOVEREIGNTY

Okay, now to deal with God's "atrociousness." God's nature is also why you can't compare Him to anything here on Earth, because He made everything! For example, I could buy a bunch of rabbits (or, with my current ones, just get one male and wait a few months ) and take care of them. They are my rabbits; after all, I bought them and fed/am feeding them. So I have the right to buy a bunch of cement blocks to partition their living spaces and the places they can dig, if I indeed do put them over grass/dirt at all instead of in cages. I also have the right to slit their jugulars and cook them and eat them if I ever want/need to. However, I do not have the right to purposely prolong such suffering while slaughtering them, or intentionally, maliciously throw bricks at them or cut off a leg/ear or gouge out an eye. Why is this? I own them in the sense that I do provide food, water, and safe shelter for them, I take out their trash, and so on, but they're not my "own"I mean, not in the same sense that I used when I declared above, "they are my rabbits."

Hm...

... In fact, I don't think there's quite a term in the English language to exactly define total ownership, which is probably because the Lord alone bears it; I still must respect them for what they arebeautiful creations of God, so I'm not allowed to abuse them. (I think there are verses that specifically state this, even, though I can't find any at the moment. The passage below is more important and encompassing anyways.) Paul explains God's complete dominion over all things very well:

Romans 9:10-21

Not only that, but Rebekah's children had one and the same father, our father Isaac. Yet, before the twins were born or had done anything good or badin order that God's purpose in election might stand: not by works but by him who callsshe was told, "The older will serve the younger."[d] Just as it is written: "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated."[e]

What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Not at all! For he says to Moses,
   "I will have mercy on whom I have mercy,
      and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion."[f]
It does not, therefore, depend on man's desire or effort, but on God's mercy. For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: "I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display my power in you and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth."[g] Therefore God has mercy on whom he wants to have mercy, and he hardens whom he wants to harden.

 One of you will say to me: "Then why does God still blame us? For who resists his will?" But who are you, O man, to talk back to God? "Shall what is formed say to him who formed it, 'Why did you make me like this?' "[h] Does not the potter have the right to make out of the same lump of clay some pottery for noble purposes and some for common use?

[d] Gen. 25:23
[e] Mal. 1:2,3
[f] Exodus 33:19
[g] Exodus 9:16
[h] Isaiah 29:16; 45:9
The last verse is pretty much the center of it all. God literally formed <i>everything</i> about us. When it boils down to the raw core, He ultimately created us out of pure <i>nothingness</i>, which gives him absolute sovereignty over everything that has ever existed.

Maximize freedom. Stop tyrannies and monopolies, of course, but let everything else roam free.
